stem: On a city map drawn on a coordinate grid, Main Street lies along the line \(2x - y = 3\). A new street will pass through the library at the point \((6, 1)\) and will be perpendicular to Main Street. At which point will the new street cross the \(y\)-axis?
solution: Main Street is \(y = 2x - 3\), with slope 2. The new street has slope \(-\frac{1}{2}\).
The new street crosses the \(y\)-axis at \((0, 4)\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This uses slope \(-2\), which changes the sign but does not take the reciprocal.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the \(y\)-intercept of the line through \((6, 1)\) with slope 2, which is parallel to Main Street.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This uses slope \(\frac{1}{2}\); a perpendicular slope must also have the opposite sign.

verify:
choices = {o: choices[n] for o, n in {'D': 'A', 'B': 'B', 'A': 'C', 'C': 'D'}.items()}; answer = {'A': 'D', 'B': 'B', 'C': 'A', 'D': 'C'}[answer]  # shuffled: original letters
x, y = symbols('x y')
pt = lambda s: [value(t) for t in s.replace('\\(', '').replace('\\)', '').strip()[1:-1].split(',')]
m0 = diff(solve(Eq(2*x - y, 3), y)[0], x)
line = -1/m0*(x - 6) + 1
yi = line.subs(x, 0)
assert yi == 4
ok = [k for k in choices if pt(choices[k]) == [0, yi]]
assert ok == [answer]
